analysis.evidence: Pharaoh is the caller, and לְאַבְרָם identifies Abram as the person he summons. The following וַיֹּאמֶר introduces Pharaoh’s questions to Abram.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ marks the narrative sequence. The verb is Qal wayyiqtol, third-person masculine singular, with Pharaoh as its subject.

draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: וַיִּקְרָא פַרְעֹה לְאַבְרָם means “Pharaoh called for Abram.” Pharaoh then addresses Abram directly, asking why he did not say that she was his wife.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לְ marks Abram, a personal name, as the person Pharaoh calls.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: In לָמָּה לֹא הִגַּדְתָּ לִּי, “Why did you not tell me?”, לֹא negates הִגַּדְתָּ, “you told.” Pharaoh asks why Abram failed to tell him that she was Abram’s wife.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew negative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Pharaoh asks Abram, “Why didn’t you tell me that she was your wife?” לִּי identifies Pharaoh as the recipient, and כִּי אִשְׁתְּךָ הִוא gives the fact Abram failed to report.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil perfect, second person masculine singular. The ending ־תָּ marks Abram as the person addressed.
analysis.sense: tell someone that something is the case

analysis.evidence: In לָמָּה לֹא הִגַּדְתָּ לִּי כִּי אִשְׁתְּךָ הִוא, “Why did you not tell me that she is your wife?”, כִּי introduces the statement Pharaoh expected Abram to tell him.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew conjunction with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: that (what is seen, known or said)
